transcript.text: Alright everyone, before I sign off on the checkout cluster's autoscaling and operating policy for the upcoming production traffic cycle, I need to hear from each of you. We've got the cluster scaling between 10 and 30 nodes with automatic consolidation, and it's passed routine availability tests with Monday morning's traffic cycle coming up. Per our standard review process, I need reliability, finance, checkout operations, and security to report any constraints or concerns before I give final approval. What are you each seeing?

transcript.text: During an overnight load replay yesterday, I measured that checkout latency breaches its 300 ms target whenever the workload has fewer than 18 nodes. I haven't filed this measurement yet because the replay was part of a separate reliability investigation, but it's directly relevant here: our current minimum of 10 nodes would not meet the latency target under production load conditions.

This means the autoscaling policy needs to ensure pods are constrained to the hardened node pool before I can sign off from a security perspective.

Process the finance correction ticket to formally update the approved cost model to reflect the 24-node maximum.
